title: Exercise 4: Multiply Two Rational Expressions
description: Practice multiplying rational expressions by canceling a common factor and simplifying the remaining numerical coefficient.
instructions: Arithmetic Level 2 is allowed. This permits nested sums and products, the negative unit, and simple nonnegative whole-number exponents.
Treat each denominator as an inverse. A displayed unit fraction such as 1/6 means inverse(6), not 1 multiplied by inverse(6).
Cancel x + 4 with inverse(x + 4), factor 6 as 2 times 3, distribute the inverse across that product, and cancel 3 with inverse(3).
Assume every denominator is nonzero; here x is not equal to -4.
